verdicts.note: Byte-exact at :310. `rankingKeyFor` is at :70-72 and returns `spark.arcade.${boardId}.ranking.v1`. Per-browser, per-machine. The inference (an unshared board correctly shows the brother nothing) holds.

verdicts.note: Byte-exact. `getLeaderboard()` at :498-500 is the single consumer and caches the choice; `selectLeaderboard` is the only other caller and is test-only. There is no second selection site.

verdicts.claim: arcadeLeaderboard.ts:359 — `if (!res.ok) return null;` collapses 403/404/429/500/503 into the same null as offline; :388-390 catches the rest
verdicts.note: Byte-exact at :359. :388 `} catch {` / :389 `return null; // offline, DNS, CORS, abort, non-JSON — one answer: use the offline tier`. The design intent is stated at :244-248 (quote verified verbatim: 'The recap is the last thing a player sees after a good run; it is the worst possible place to surface a network error'). verdicts.claim: arcadeRunOverlay.ts:306 — the grey caption is the ONLY on-screen difference between a live shared board and a dead one
verdicts.note: The line is byte-exact at :306. But it is not the only signal: :329 prints 'NO RANKING YET' when `rows.length === 0`, and :285 prints 'RUN n — INCLUDING k SAVED OFFLINE' when `flushed > 0`. More important — the caption is a TOLERANT TERNARY (`shared === true ? … : …`), which is exactly the S182-lesson-7 hiding place for the new `why` union the researcher proposes. See `missed`.

verdicts.claim: arcadeLeaderboard.ts:354 — `runs: runs.map((r) => ({ name: r.name, ms: r.ms, id: r.id })),` means every browser submit carries an id; a curl never does
verdicts.note: The line and :296 (`const thisRun: PendingRun = { name, ms, id: newRunId(), at: Date.now() };`) are byte-exact, and worker.js:412/:416/:434-435 behave as described. But the conclusion drawn from it — that the live `seen_runs` path was never exercised — is REFUTED by the repo's own record. See the next row.

verdicts.claim: worker.js:416 SELECT against `seen_runs` may throw on a live D1 that never got the 41b0da6 migration; the 'Verified live' claims in that commit could not have touched that table
verdicts.note: ⛔ THIS IS THE REPORT'S CENTRAL ERROR. The line is byte-exact, but `git log -1 --format=%B 41b0da6` states, in its own body: 'Verified live: replaying two ids returned duplicates=2 with the average unchanged' and '⚠ ONE FAILED COMMAND, RULED AND RESOLVED: `wrangler d1 execute --file` returned "Authentication error [code: 10000]" … Applied the new table via `--command` instead and confirmed `seen_runs` exists.' `duplicates` is computed at worker.js:422-423 as `runs.length - foldable.length`, and `foldable` filters on the Set populated ONLY by the :414-419 SELECT — so `duplicates=2` is arithmetically unreachable unless that table existed and that SELECT ran, with ids, live. The researcher asserted a negative the tree contradicts, and did so without opening the commit message he cited.

verdicts.claim: e2e.yml:543 — no CI job deploys the worker or applies the schema; package.json:7-28 has no wrangler script
verdicts.note: e2e.yml:543 byte-exact ('bundle — it runs on Cloudflare, ships by `wrangler deploy`, and nothing about it can affect the'). package.json scripts run :8-:28 and contain no wrangler invocation. The structural observation stands even though its concrete instantiation (the seen_runs gap) is refuted — the server genuinely is versioned by hand, and fix D is the right artefact.

verdicts.claim: server.worker.test.ts:24 — `function makeDb(...)` is an in-memory mock, so the suite is green whatever the live D1 contains
verdicts.note: Byte-exact at :24, and :55-61 do model the `seen_runs` SELECT and the `INSERT OR IGNORE`. But framing this as an undiscovered blind spot overstates: the file's own docblock at :10-13 says it outright — 'it is not a database, so it cannot prove a query is correct — the live checks do that.' The limitation is documented and its compensating control is named. It is also true of every unit suite against any remote DB.

verdicts.claim: arcadeScores.ts:401 PENDING_MAX_AGE_MS = 12h; prunePending at :422-427 expired his 09-18 runs on the morning of 09-19
verdicts.note: Byte-exact at :401, and :426 is `return pending.filter((r) => Math.abs(now - r.at) < PENDING_MAX_AGE_MS);`. Canon §9's caveat (SPARK_CANON.md:446-467) blesses the raise-SEEN_RUN_TTL_MS fix verbatim. verdicts.note: `rejected,` byte-exact at :485; `duplicates` beside it. worker.js:350 `return json({ error: 'slow down', rows: await readBoard(env, board) }, 429, origin);` — and arcadeLeaderboard.ts:360-387 reads only `rows` and `you`. missed: ⛔ THE CHEAPEST PROBE ALREADY EXISTS IN CI AND THE REPORT NEVER MENTIONS IT. deploy.yml:180-182 runs a step named 'Leaderboard wiring report (never fails the build)' → `node scripts/leaderboard-wiring-report.mjs` with `VITE_LEADERBOARD_URL` in its env. That script (:60-84) prints exactly one of three verdicts: `VITE_LEADERBOARD_URL: not set` / `SET but UNUSABLE` + the specific reason / `✅ SHARED BOARD WILL BE SHIPPED`. server/leaderboard/README.md:139-141 says so in as many words: 'Read that block — it is the only thing that distinguishes a working board from the original bug.' H2 is answered by `gh run view <last deploy> --log | grep -A6 'SPARK leaderboard wiring'` — no curl, no live asset fetch, and it is dated per-deploy. The report calls H2 'a property of the deployed asset [that] cannot be settled from the tree' while the tree contains the machine that logs it.

⛔ THE REPORT'S OWN STEP-1 PROBE IS UNSOUND AND ITS STATED VERDICT IS A FALSE NEGATIVE. `curl … | grep -c 'spark-leaderboard'` returns 0 whenever the worker is behind anything other than that hostname — and README.md:130-133 explicitly contemplates the move: 'if the board ever matters more, put it behind a custom domain. The client accepts any https origin, so that move is a variable change and nothing else.' The report then says '**A count of 0 means the live bundle has no worker URL**', which would send the whole fix down the wrong branch. Grep for `/board/` (the literal in the template at arcadeLeaderboard.ts:349) or read the deploy log instead.

⭐ A FOURTH ROOT CAUSE, SELF-CONSISTENT, NEEDING NO MISCONFIGURATION AT ALL — and the report buries it as 'H4 is mostly NOT the cause'. If the owner's runs were rejected by MIN_MS (worker.js:70, 15 s), the server folds nothing, `readPlayer` returns null, `you` is null, and `withOwnRow` (arcadeLeaderboard.ts:203-217) hits its third arm: `const local = entryOf(localCache, name); return local === null ? [...entries] : [...entries, local];` — it re-attaches the LOCAL row. So the owner sees himself on the board, sees the green 'everyone · by average time' caption, and has no idea the `players` table is empty. His brother, on a perfectly healthy and correctly-wired shared board, then sees only himself. THAT REPRODUCES THE EXACT REPORT WITH NOTHING BROKEN. ⚠ Calibration the report also owed and did not do: src/state/sudoku.ts:23 states the measured band — '~16 of 36 reads as a real puzzle, **~30–90s solve**' — and :49-51 adds that at 16 givens '100% of puzzles fall to naked singles alone'. The floor is half the measured lower bound, which makes this less likely than a fast solver suggests but is a number the report should have quoted before asking the owner for it.

⛔ A PERMANENT CLIENT/SERVER DIVERGENCE THE REPORT DOES NOT NAME, in the same `withOwnRow` arm. The local fold happens BEFORE the await (arcadeLeaderboard.ts:268 `saveRanking(foldRun(before, name, ms), boardId);`). On a 200 where the run was MIN_MS-rejected and the player is outside the top 25, `withOwnRow`'s fallback keeps the locally-folded row forever. The player's local average permanently includes a run the shared board refused, and nothing ever reconciles it. Fix C must either unwind the local fold when `rejected > 0` and `you` is null, or state the divergence — otherwise surfacing `rejected` tells the player about a run their own screen is still counting.

⛔ THE TOLERANT DEFAULT, exactly per S182 lesson 7, and it is the ternary the report cites as its own evidence. arcadeRunOverlay.ts:306 is `run.update?.shared === true ? 'everyone …' : 'this device only …'` and :178 is `shared: run.update?.shared ?? false`. Anything that is not literally `true` reads as 'this device only'. If fix A keeps the 429 rows (as it proposes) and the implementer sets `shared: true` because the server DID answer, the caption says 'everyone' for a run that was NOT folded. And if `why`/`queued` are added as OPTIONAL fields, tsc catches nothing anywhere. ⭐ Make them REQUIRED on `RankingUpdate` — that is what forces every construction site to be visited.

⭐ A FOURTH ORDERING SITE the determinism_risk section misses. It names `compareRows` (arcadeScores.ts:169-173), worker `rankRows` (worker.js:178-190) and the truePlace COUNT (worker.js:468-477) — but schema.sql:45-48 carries `idx_players_rank` with the comment 'The ordering expression must match `compareRows` in src/render/arcadeScores.ts: average ASC, then runs DESC, then name ASC.' That is FOUR sites, not three. Also worth knowing before anyone 'optimises': `readBoard` (worker.js:223-229) does a bare `SELECT … WHERE board = ?1` with NO `ORDER BY` and sorts in JS, so that index is currently ornamental.

⚠ `ArcadeRunUiPoints` HAS ITS OWN FOUR SITES and the report names two of them, with wrong line numbers. A new snapshot field needs: the interface (arcadeRunOverlay.ts:~81), **the `BLANK` literal at :85-86** (which the report does not mention — `this.last = { ...BLANK, … }` at :135 spreads it, so an omitted field is silently undefined on the hidden branch), the `this.last = {…}` write at :165-179, and every `getUiPoints()` consumer. ⚠ The report's citations here are wrong: `private last` is at :105 (not :86 — :86 is the BLANK literal), and the writes are at :135 and :165 (not :174).

⚠ THERE *IS* AN ARCADE E2E TEST IN THE GATING LANE, contradicting tests_owed #3's 'there is no e2e lane covering the arcade board at all'. `e2e/zones-visual.spec.ts:329` — `test.describe('@visual S149 P5 — arcade mode on screen', …)`. `@visual` is NOT in `e2e:gating`'s grep-invert list (package.json:18 inverts only `@quarantine-flaky|@soak|@perf-measure|@archived-hazard|@races`), so it gates. It stops at the puzzle launch and never reaches RECAP/BOARD — so the report's point survives for the BOARD — but a branch touching the overlay's container stacking or the title layout can red it, and it must be in the brief.

⭐ A DEAD EXPORT THAT IS THE NATURAL HOOK FOR FIX A. `isSharedBoardConfigured()` (arcadeLeaderboard.ts:509-511) has ZERO production call sites — grep across `src --include=*.ts` minus tests returns only its own declaration and its own docblock. Fix A's `'not-configured'` discriminant is already computable; the function just needs a consumer. The report proposes inventing the signal without noticing the predicate exists.

⚠ A BOUNDARY THAT IS EXACTLY TIGHT AND WOULD BREAK SILENTLY. `FLUSH_BATCH = 20` (arcadeLeaderboard.ts:239) + the current run = 21 runs per POST, and `MAX_RUNS_PER_REQUEST = 21` (worker.js:98). One more queued run per batch and `parseRuns` returns `{error:'too many runs'}` → 400 → `!res.ok` → null → the queue never drains. Any branch touching the flush path must know these two constants are joined and unpinned by any test.

⚠ A FIFTH SCHEMA-TOUCHING COMMIT THE REPORT DOES NOT LIST. It names e1fe909 / 24d5a41 / 41b0da6 and stops at 2026-09-18 22:55. `git log -- server/leaderboard/schema.sql` also returns **a765331 (2026-09-19 11:43, today)**. I checked the diff: comments only (and in worker.js the only non-comment change is `const SEEN_RUN_TTL_MS` → `export const SEEN_RUN_TTL_MS`). So no migration is owed — but a report whose central claim is 'somebody has to run the migrations' must enumerate the migration commits completely, and this one was missed.

⚠ A 403-ORIGIN PATH THE REPORT MENTIONS BUT DOES NOT ENUMERATE. worker.js:39 is `const ALLOWED_ORIGINS = new Set(['https://spark-online.space']);` and `public/CNAME` is exactly `spark-online.space`. Any other host the game is reachable on — a `www.` variant, or the raw `*.github.io` Pages URL, which GitHub keeps live — presents a different Origin, `corsHeaders` (worker.js:191-192) then answers with `access-control-allow-origin: https://spark-online.space`, the browser rejects before the client can read the status, and the catch at :388 makes it indistinguishable from offline. If the brother opened the github.io link, that alone is the whole bug. Worth one question to the owner: which URL did he open?

⚠ DETERMINISM CHECK, INDEPENDENTLY RUN AND AGREED. `grep -rn "from './arcadeScores\|arcadeLeaderboard.ts'" src --include=*.ts` minus tests returns only arcadeLeaderboard.ts:70, arcadeRun.ts:36/:41 and arcadeRunOverlay.ts:39 — all under `src/render/`. The report's determinism_risk is correct.

size_grade: DISAGREE — the report grades Standard (10-30K) with a hedge to Full; the honest grade is **Full (>30K)**, and it should be briefed as Full from the start. Three things the estimate does not price. (1) `src/ci.leaderboardGate.test.ts` is 455 lines of source-text guards covering ten different files including package.json and README.md — both of which fixes D and F edit. That file has to be READ, not skimmed, before either edit, and tests_owed #6 adds a new mechanical enumeration to it on top. (2) Making `why`/`queued` required on `RankingUpdate` (which is the right call — see `missed`) ripples through four test files and both client classes, and the report's file_set names only three of them. (3) The probe step is a live-ops diagnosis with a genuinely branching outcome, and the report's own probe is unsound, so the branch inherits the work of designing a correct one. Against that, one thing pulls the other way and should be said plainly: the report's biggest single work item — fix D's migration/deploy path — is justified as hygiene but NOT as this bug's cause, because 41b0da6's record shows `seen_runs` live. If the wiring-report log (see `missed`) says `not set`, the actual fix is `gh variable set` plus a push, and the session collapses to a Micro doc-and-signal pass. ⭐ SO: brief it Full, but put the log read FIRST and re-tier after it.
net_assessment: ⭐ STRONG REPORT, ONE LOAD-BEARING ERROR, AND A BETTER PROBE SITTING UNREAD IN THE REPO. Eleven of twelve evidence lines are byte-exact where cited and mean what the claim says — unusually good for this project. The H1 refutation is correct and correctly reasoned (arcadeRun.ts:172-175, main.ts:1459 and :1495-1496 all verify exactly), and it is right to say DO NOT TOUCH the reveal gate: that is R182-G, SPARK_CANON.md:429 'gated on submission … an anti-griefing measure, not a UI flourish'. Nothing in fixes A–F breaks a canon ruling. The average-not-best-time model, name-as-identity, sum-and-count storage and the run-1 ranking are all left alone; fix E is explicitly blessed by canon §9's own caveat at :464-467 ('A better fix exists and is cheap: raise SEEN_RUN_TTL_MS'). No archived subsystem is reported as live. determinism_risk is right and I verified it independently. ⛔ THE ONE THING THAT MUST NOT SURVIVE INTO THE BRIEF is defect (2)'s narrative. 'If `seen_runs` was never created on the live D1, every real browser submit 500s while a curl passes' is a real hazard CLASS, but its instantiation is refuted by the repo's own record: 41b0da6's commit body reports `duplicates=2` from replaying two ids live, a number that is arithmetically unreachable without that table and that SELECT, and separately states 'confirmed `seen_runs` exists'. The report asserts the opposite — that those 'Verified live' claims 'could not have touched that table' — without opening the message it cites. A branch that starts by re-running migrations against a live D1 on that premise is doing owner-facing work on a false one. ⛔ AND THE DIAGNOSIS IS OVER-BUILT FOR THE QUESTION. deploy.yml:180-182 already runs `scripts/leaderboard-wiring-report.mjs`, whose three verdicts are the literal answer to H2, and README.md:139-141 says reading that block is 'the only thing that distinguishes a working board from the original bug'. That is one `gh run view`, it is dated, and it cannot false-negative the way the report's `grep -c 'spark-leaderboard'` can. ⭐ WHAT I WOULD ADD TO THE BRIEF, IN ORDER: read the wiring-report block from the last deploy; ask the owner which URL his brother opened (worker.js:39 allows exactly `https://spark-online.space`, and a github.io or www. host is a silent 403 that looks identical); then weigh MIN_MS properly — `withOwnRow`'s local-cache fallback (arcadeLeaderboard.ts:214-216) means a player whose runs are all rejected sees a green 'everyone' caption and himself on the board while the server's table stays empty, which reproduces this report end to end with nothing misconfigured. ⭐ FIXES A, B, C AND F ARE RIGHT WHATEVER THE PROBE SAYS and should be briefed as unconditional — with `why`/`queued` REQUIRED, not optional, and with the ternary at arcadeRunOverlay.ts:306 named in the brief as the tolerant default that will otherwise swallow the new union exactly as S182 lesson 7 predicts.
